Olga/Laura — quick product note on operational behavior and feasible mitigations.

Summary of current default telemetry (short):
- Inference request logs: request metadata (timestamp, model id, token counts, latency) are stored in our observability pipeline.
- Sampled prompt traces: by default we sample ~0.1% of requests for quality debugging; sampled traces include prompt and model output.
- KV/prefix cache: KV cache lives in GPU process memory and ephemeral local caches; we persist periodic snapshots for warm-start (configurable per deployment). Snapshots do not include customer PII extraction by default but can contain unredacted prompt text if a sampled trace captured it.

What we can offer as guardrails for Helix:
1) Telemetry opt-out: a tenant-level flag to disable sampled prompt traces for Helix (no sampled prompt content leaves the tenant environment).
2) Retention window: set telemetry retention to 30 days for Helix observability tables; older records auto-purged.
3) Prompt redaction: implement a production redaction pipeline to redact email addresses, SSNs, and credit-card patterns from sampled traces before they persist. We can roll this in as a short-term fix (2–3 weeks) or backfill existing samples if needed.
4) No-training guarantee: we can operationally ensure runtime inputs/outputs are not used for model training for Helix by flagging their tenant in our internal tooling and excluding their data from any training pipelines.

Open questions for Security/Legal: is redact+opt-out sufficient, or does Helix require absolute guarantee that no raw prompts are written to any subprocessor? If yes, we should enumerate which subprocessors (logging providers, analytics) would need contracts amended.

I'll draft a one-paragraph product-friendly clause you can put into the DPA if the above is acceptable.

—Dylan

Thanks, Dylan. Security perspective below.

Concerns and suggested controls:
- Raw prompt persistence: the primary risk is sampled traces that include user prompts being sent to downstream analytics/logging subprocessors (we use LogStream and MetricsLab). If Helix requires that no raw prompts are persisted by any subprocessor, we must ensure the telemetry opt-out extends end-to-end (ingest -> exporter).
- Redaction efficacy: regex redaction will catch common patterns (emails, SSNs, credit cards) but not all PII (free text names, medical details). Propose a hybrid approach: regex + PII detector with confidence threshold, and an allowlist for Helix-only fields that may be captured.
- Retention: 30 days is reasonable as a default. We recommend adding a right-to-request immediate purge clause for Helix (incident-driven) and an automated deletion flow for tenant-scoped snapshots.
- Subprocessor commitments: we will need to confirm LogStream and MetricsLab retention & deletion support and whether they store raw payloads in any long-term tier. If they do, we need contractual assurances or to implement tenant-level filtering before export.

Suggested DPA redline snippet (high level, for Legal to refine):
"Redwood shall not use Customer runtime inputs or outputs for model training or to improve model weights without Customer's explicit written consent. For Customer tenants who request, Redwood will: (i) disable sampled prompt traces for that tenant; (ii) restrict telemetry retention to a configurable window not to exceed 30 days by default; and (iii) implement prompt redaction and PII filtering prior to export to any subprocessor. Redwood will provide a list of subprocessors that may receive telemetry and will contractually require those subprocessors to honor Customer-specific data retention and deletion requests."

Operational ask: product/support needs a tenant flag to disable sampled prompt exports and an API to request immediate purge. If Product confirms those exist or can be implemented in ~2–3 weeks, Security can accept the above language.

—Soojin Lee
Senior Security Engineer | Redwood Inference

Emma — thanks for the clear asks. Copying our product, security and legal leads so you have a single-threaded response. Below is the operational summary Redwood can commit to for Helix, subject to contract language to be drafted by our legal team: 

Agreed items (summary):
- No-training guarantee: Redwood will not use Helix runtime inputs or outputs to train models or improve model weights without Helix's explicit written consent.
- Telemetry opt-out: We will provide a tenant-level flag to disable sampled prompt traces for Helix so that no sampled prompt content is exported from their tenant environment.
- Redaction & PII filtering: Redwood will implement prompt redaction (regex + PII detector) prior to persisting or exporting sampled traces.
- Retention window: Telemetry retention for Helix will be set to a maximum of 30 days by default; Helix will have the right to request immediate purge of tenant-scoped telemetry.
- Subprocessor list & commitments: We will produce a list of telemetry subprocessors (LogStream, MetricsLab) and add contract language requiring them to honor Helix-specific retention and deletion requests for the telemetry they receive.

Next steps:
1) Legal (Laura): please draft the DPA amendment language reflecting the agreed items and attach the updated PDF.
2) Product (Dylan): confirm feasibility and ETA for tenant flag + purge API (Dylan suggested 2–3 weeks if prioritized). Please call out any limitations for Dedicated/Private deployments.
3) Security (Soojin): validate redaction approach and confirm which subprocessors require contractual updates.
4) Marcus/CS: let Helix know we can provide a tracked DocuSign amendment once legal drafts the wording.

Emma — I'm attaching a draft one-paragraph we can include for immediate review and a DocuSign link placeholder. If Helix legal agrees on the wording below, we can issue an updated PDF and start the sign path.

Draft paragraph (for Helix review):
"Redwood will not use Customer runtime inputs or outputs for model training or to improve model weights without the Customer’s explicit written consent. Upon Customer request, Redwood will: (a) disable sampled prompt export for the Customer tenant; (b) apply prompt redaction and PII filtering prior to persisting or exporting telemetry; (c) limit telemetry retention for that tenant to a maximum of 30 days and honor Customer-initiated purge requests; and (d) require any subprocessor receiving telemetry to comply with Customer-specific retention and deletion instructions."

Please let us know if that captures Helix's needs or if you'd like any of the controls tightened. We'll aim to have a contract-ready amendment by EOW if Product can deliver the tenant flag/purge API timeline.

Best,
